APPLE, HUMAN INTERFACE Three zones only: one hero, one grid, one quiet strip. Anything that wanted a fourth zone got folded into the strip.
ITUNES, LIBRARY ERA The square cover is the module. Tabs, hero and strip all align to the same 132px column so the page reads as one grid, not four panels.
SPOTIFY, DESIGN LEAD Tools become a horizontal action strip under the search bar. A sidebar list is where features go to die.
CONTRAST SCIENCE Three states, three shapes, three words: filled check for Banked, outlined square for Needs work, dashed circle for Not started. Hue is decoration on top.

Reading a lead sheet

TEACH3 of 7
WHEN YOU ARE READY

A lead sheet gives you the melody and the chord symbols, and nothing else. Your left hand decides what the harmony sounds like. Start by playing only the root of each symbol on beat one, then add the rest of the chord once the changes feel automatic.

  1. Play the melody alone, right hand, one time through.
  2. Say each chord symbol out loud on beat one.
  3. Add the root in the left hand, nothing else.
  4. Fill in the full chord under the melody.

No video for this step. The written steps and the keyboard are the whole lesson.

Section B, clean

RESULTS
NOTES236/240TIMING+14msMISSED4TIERhard
  • Bars 21 to 24 slowed by 8 bpm against the click.
  • Left hand landed late on every Fmaj7.
  • Dynamics stayed flat from bar 17 onward.

One more clean run at this tempo banks the day.

Why Fmaj7 sits under that melody

The melody note is E, the seventh of F. Playing a plain F triad under it leaves the E unsupported, so the arrangement uses Fmaj7 and the note becomes part of the chord instead of a passing tone.

Seen. It will come back as a drill on Thursday.

The dashed 393px fold line on each screen marks what you would see without scrolling, at your real window size. On a phone this is a scaled-down preview, not a mobile design: the whole 756px screen is shrunk to fit, so a 44px control lands at about 21px. Pinch to zoom in and read it. The app itself is desktop only, because Web MIDI does not exist on iOS, so the phone view is for looking rather than using. Every screen is the Claude Design output, lifted exactly. The row of buttons at the top is prototype scaffolding, not part of the design: the design does not draw app navigation, so this is how you walk it. Inside the Library, Free play, Metronome, Latency calibration, Start, Continue and All tools really navigate.
